title: Form validation and shortcuts
description:
Write the pure functions behind a signup form and a keyboard handler:

```javascript
function validateSignup(values) { }   // values from Object.fromEntries(new FormData(form)): all strings
function keyCommand(event) { }        // a command name for a keydown event, or null
```

`validateSignup` returns `{ ok, data, errors }`:
- `name`: trimmed, at least 2 characters, else error `"Enter at least 2 characters."`
- `email`: trimmed and lower-cased; one `@` with text before it and a `.` somewhere after it, else `"Enter a valid email."`
- `age`: optional. Empty means `null`; otherwise a whole number from 13 to 120, else `"Enter an age from 13 to 120."`
- `password`: at least 8 characters with a letter and a digit, else `"Use 8 or more characters with a letter and a digit."`
- `confirm` must equal `password`, else `"The passwords do not match."` (only checked when the password itself is valid).

`errors` has one message per bad field (an empty object when all is well), `ok` is true when there are none, and `data` holds the cleaned `{ name, email, age }` (no passwords) when `ok`, else `null`.

`keyCommand` gets `{ key, ctrlKey, metaKey, shiftKey }`, where Ctrl on Windows and Linux and Cmd (meta) on a Mac count the same, and returns:
- Ctrl/Cmd + `s`: `"save"`; Ctrl/Cmd + `z`: `"undo"`; Ctrl/Cmd + Shift + `z` or Ctrl/Cmd + `y`: `"redo"`
- `Escape` (with no modifier): `"close"`; `/` with no modifier: `"search"`
- anything else: `null`. Letters may arrive as upper case when Shift is held.
hints: Collect errors in an object as you go, so every bad field is reported at once instead of stopping at the first.

Characters compare by their code, so `c >= "0" && c <= "9"` is true exactly for a digit, and `c.toLowerCase() >= "a" && c.toLowerCase() <= "z"` for a letter. `[...password].some(...)` asks whether any character passes.
Keys like `"Escape"` are longer than one character, so lower-case only the single-character keys; then Shift + `Z` (`"Z"`) and `z` compare the same.
